title: Bridging loans total £2.51m for hotel and retail deals
summary:
Recognise Bank has completed two bridging loans totalling £2.51 million to finance the acquisition of a hotel in Southend-on-Sea and a mixed-use investment property in London. The transactions were structured to enable quick completion and provide time for refinancing arrangements.

title: Native Land secures £226m finance for Belgravia project
summary:
Developer Native Land has secured £226 million in development finance for a residential scheme in Belgravia, comprising a £160 million senior debt facility from Barclays alongside equity from Malaysia's Amcorp Group Berhad and a Qatari-based family office. The financing enables the £41 million freehold purchase of Kilmuir House and 62 South Eaton Place from Grosvenor.

title: Estate agency consultant urges firms to modernise or risk losing ground
summary:
Estate agencies must continuously update their business models or risk being overtaken by competitors who offer better customer experiences, according to Chris Webb, founder of The Estate Agent Consultancy. Webb draws parallels with Apple's decision to launch the iPhone despite it cannibalising sales of the highly successful iPod.

The post Estate agency consultant urges firms to modernise or risk losing ground appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: AI tools provide inconsistent rental property advice
summary:
A comparison of three major AI platforms has revealed significant inconsistencies in rental property advice, with each providing different guidance on costs, tenancy rules and safety checks. The research by estate agency 1st Avenue highlights concerns about relying solely on AI-generated information when searching for rental accommodation.

title: Garden maintenance disputes highlight tenant liability issues
summary:
A tenancy deposit adjudication has ruled in favour of a landlord claiming costs for garden restoration, highlighting the importance of detailed property documentation in the UK rental sector. The case underscores tenant liability for maintenance obligations specified in tenancy agreements.

The post Garden maintenance disputes highlight tenant liability issues appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK rental growth forecast to outpace house prices by 2029
summary:
Rental growth on newly agreed lets is projected to reach 14.2% between 2026 and 2029, nearly double the anticipated 7.2% increase in house prices across Britain, according to Hamptons' latest rental market forecast. The estate agency attributes the divergence to ongoing financial and regulatory pressures on landlords constraining rental property supply.

The post UK rental growth forecast to outpace house prices by 2029 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Knight Frank cuts UK house price forecast to 1% for 2027
summary:
Knight Frank has revised its UK house price forecast for 2027 downward, reducing expected growth from 3% to 1% amid mounting economic uncertainty and elevated borrowing costs. The property consultancy has also lowered its five-year growth projection to 2031 from 20.4% to 14.2%.

The post Knight Frank cuts UK house price forecast to 1% for 2027 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: UK house price growth diverges sharply across nations
summary:
House price performance across the UK's constituent nations shows significant variation, with Northern Ireland and Scotland outpacing England and Wales. Scotland's average property price reached £198,000 in August 2026, marking a 2.9% annual increase, whilst Northern Ireland recorded the strongest growth at 6.9% year-on-year.

The post UK house price growth diverges sharply across nations appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: BestAgent clarifies viewing charges amid board resignation
summary:
Property portal BestAgent has issued a statement addressing concerns over viewing charges, property listings, and anonymous comments following the resignation of Yopa chief executive Verona Frankish from its advisory board. The clarification comes after a week of criticism over the platform's business practices and handling of agent relationships.

The post BestAgent clarifies viewing charges amid board resignation appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Shawbrook provides £3.37m exit finance for Plumstead homes
summary:
Shawbrook has provided a £3.37m development exit finance facility to ID Partnership Ltd for an eight-home residential development in Plumstead, South East London. The 12-month facility operates at 70% loan-to-value against a gross development value of approximately £4.82m.
